complete_source.work: Vitruvius IX.8.8, all of the owned Gwilt English paragraph
complete_source.text: 8. Other kinds of winter-dials are made, which are called Anaporica . They are constructed as follows. With the aid of the analemma the hours are marked by brazen rods on their face, beginning from the centre, whereon circles are drawn, shewing the limits of the months. Behind these rods a wheel is placed, on which are measured and painted the heavens and the zodiac with the figures of the twelve celestial signs, by drawing lines from the centre, which mark the greater and smaller spaces of each sign. On the back part of the middle of the wheel is fixed a revolving axis, round which a pliable brass chain is coiled, at one of whose ends a phellos or tympanum hangs, which is raised by the water, and at the other end a counterpoise of sand equal to the weight of the phellos .
complete_source.boundary: From8. Other kinds of winter-dials... through ...equal to the weight of the phellos .; stops before9. Thus as...
complete_source.historical_date: Ancient work, late first century BCE; owned text is the later public-domain Gwilt English translation hosted by LacusCurtius, not a medieval witness. Exact printed edition/year and Latin variants were not collated in this bounded pass.
complete_source.edition_limit: Anaporica spelling, eighth-division references and the hydraulic explanations remain this translation branch. Physical engineering adequacy is not certified. The prior analemma construction is an explicit prerequisite outside this bounded clock description.
complete_source.old_longer_source_defect: Full§8–15 packet and§12 annotation/HTML fragment remain unchanged. Anaporica spelling retained; no Latin/medieval collation or engineering certification.

source_obligations: Other winter-dials are called Anaporica; construction account follows. The name and other-kind framing must not be silently omitted.
With aid of the prior analemma, brazen rods mark hours on the face from the centre; circles show month limits. Analemma is an explicit prior construction dependency, not a newly derived diagram.

Behind those rods is W bearing measured/painted heavens and zodiac with figures of twelve celestial signs; centre-drawn lines mark greater/smaller spaces of each sign. Twelve is in the source, but any target numeral guess remains unconfirmed; no twelve-name list.
A revolving X is fixed at the back middle of that same W.

A pliable brass chain coils around X; from one end hangs a phellos or tympanum, raised by water, and from the other a sand counterpoise equal to its weight. Preserve the alternate float/tympanum naming and distinct chain ends, not merely a generic mechanism.
